# Érōs, spelled the way the sources wrote it
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *eros*. This is the file on how **Érōs** replaced it.

Érōs stands at the beginning in Hesiod and at the margins in Homer. He is one of the oldest gods, yet his stories are few — because his power is everywhere. Hesiod places Érōs fourth in the procession of being: after Cháos, Gaia, and Tartarus, but before the children of Night.  "He is the most beautiful among the immortal gods," Hesiod writes, "he makes the limbs go limp and overcomes the intelligence and prudent counsel in the breasts of all gods and men" (Theogony 120–122).

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Érōs
- **ASCII form:** eros
- **Meaning:** "Love, desire (from ἔραμαι)"
- **Domain of influence:** Love, Desire, Attraction
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Ἔρως
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 78 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Ἔρως**. On the evidence, it means "Love, desire (from ἔραμαι)".

Strip **Érōs** to *eros* and 2 pieces of evidence vanish:

- **e → É** — Epsilon with acute: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.
- **o → ō** — Omega: long omicron: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Érōs** lives at [/sites/eros/](/sites/eros/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/eros/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/eros/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/eros/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Érōs** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Love, Dating & Relationships** — Desire itself; the arrow in every match.
- **Beauty, Fashion & Cosmetics** — Desire as the engine of attraction marketing.
- **Mental Health & Emotional Wellness** — Freud made Eros the name of the life drive; psychoanalysis runs on his energy.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
